title: Borrowing Base Shortfall Paydowns on Operating Lines of Credit
content:
A member may ask to pay down one of their Operating Lines of Credit by what is needed to bring it back within its borrowing base.

## Rule

When a member asks to pay down an operating line by what is needed to bring it back within its borrowing base, the paydown is a principal payment debited from the member's own checking account on the member's own authorisation, in the amount worked out for the shortfall, and it is made within the product's deficiency cure period, in calendar days, after the certificate's received date, that date being day 0.

The shortfall paydown is not fixed until the association has worked out its own borrowing base for the line's most recent certificate and recorded it in place of the member's own figure.

The shortfall paydown is fixed only after an overadvance fee stands against the line's latest advance whenever that advance took the line past its available credit.

## Business effect

The paydown is booked as one principal payment received by phone and lowers the line's outstanding principal by its amount. The member then sees the paydown in the line's transaction history and the lower principal on the line.

## Platform reference: `authorize_shortfall_paydown_62bf68fd`

**Capability.** The member authorises a one-time debit of their own checking account for a principal paydown on one of their operating lines. One call books one principal payment of the stated amount, received today by phone, and lowers the line's outstanding principal by that amount.

**How it is invoked.** This is the member's own tool. The servicing representative unlocks `authorize_shortfall_paydown_62bf68fd` and hands it over; the customer themselves runs it, since the debit rests on the member's own authorisation.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `line_id` | Loan number of the member's operating line the paydown is applied to, as the servicing representative reads it out from the member's operating lines | Identifier |
| `amount` | The principal paydown being debited | USD, always positive, 2 decimal places, rounded half up to cents before it is passed |

**Return.** A receipt rendered as text with `txn_id` (reference number of the principal payment), `line_id` (the line paid down), `amount` (the USD paydown, 2 decimal places), `effective_date` (today's date, in year-month-day form), `outstanding_principal` (the line's principal after the paydown, USD, 2 decimal places) and `status`, the literal "applied", meaning the paydown is on the line.

## Contract questions

**Through which channel is the paydown booked?** As a principal payment received by phone, dated the day the member runs the tool.

**Who runs the debit?** The customer themselves, on their own authorisation.
